promptLatex: A bag holds $3$ red marbles and $5$ green marbles. Two marbles are drawn one at a time without replacement. The first marble drawn is red. What is the probability that the second marble drawn is green?
hintLatex: Once the red marble is out of the bag, the remaining collection is what the second draw works from.
There are $9$ marbles left, of which $5$ are still green.
solutionLatex:
The first draw removed a red marble, so $9$ marbles remain in the bag: $2$ red and $5$ green.

The second draw is now uniform over those $9$ marbles, so the sample space for the second draw has $9$ members, of which $5$ are green.

Therefore $P(\text{second is green} \mid \text{first is red}) = \frac{5}{9}$. Note that this is larger than $\frac{5}{8}$, the unconditional chance of green, because knowing a red was removed made green more likely.
